paragraphs.text: After fourscore years of peace and rest. {Jdg 3:30} The sedentary life is most subject to diseases: standing waters soon putrify. It is hard and happy not to grow worse with liberty.
paragraphs.anchor: And the children of Israel again did evil.

paragraphs.text: As Jdg 2:14. It must not be troublesome to us to hear the same things often: Verba toties repetita viva sunt, vera sunt, sans sunt, plana sunt, saith Augustine.
paragraphs.anchor: And the Lord sold them.

paragraphs.text: Whose father or grandfather, of the same name, Joshua had slain, and burnt his city. {Jos 11:1; Jos 11:11} He therefore, on revenge, having got now the better of the Israelites, oppressed them most grievously for twenty years together, using them like beasts which are bought and sold to carry burdens, as Ferus noteth.
paragraphs.anchor: Into the hand of Jabin.

paragraphs.text: Or, In the wood of the nations, {a} as some render it; that is, of the remaining Canaanites, who had hither betaken themselves for safety and conveniency of issuing forth against the enemy.
paragraphs.anchor: Which dwelt in Harosheth of the Gentiles.

paragraphs.text: {a} In loco sylvatico. Jun.
See Jdg 4:2. In the Canaanites the same wickedness prospereth that is punished in Israel. Our very profession hurteth us, if we be not innocent.
paragraphs.anchor: He mightily oppressed the children of Israel.

paragraphs.text: Or, A woman of Lapidoth, {a} or a woman of lights, - so some render it, taking the word appellatively, - so called either because concinnabat ellychnia, she made lights for the sanctuary; {b} or because she was full of heavenly lights, by the Spirit. {c}
paragraphs.anchor: The wife of Lapidoth.

paragraphs.text: {a} Lapidothana.
{b} Tremel.
{c} Vatab.

Or, She sat under the palm tree, as the Septuagint and Vulgate render it. The kings of Persia sat under a golden plane tree, or under a vine of gold, that had bunches of smaragdes and other precious stones, when they sat in judgment {a}
paragraphs.anchor: And she dwelt under the palm tree of Deborah.

paragraphs.text: “ O curas hominum! o quantum est in rebus inane! ”
{a} Athenaeus, lib. xii.

She sent; not went: for, (1.) She was a judge in Israel, and of great authority; (2.) It is not fit for women to wander up and down. Ambrose saith Barak was her son, others her husband, but neither is likely.
paragraphs.anchor: And she sent and called Barak.

paragraphs.text: In which tribe Hazor stood; and therefore their oppression was the greater. But ten thousand were but a few to go against so potent an enemy. {a} God can save with a little help. {Dan 11:34}
paragraphs.anchor: Ten thousand men of the children of Naphtali.

paragraphs.text: {a} Mashac, est occulto impetu aliquem impellere quo velis.
And I will draw unto thee … Sisera.] Verbis pelliciam, I will persuade, I will incline his heart.
“ Ducunt volentem fata, nolentem trahunt. ”

He is famous for his faith, {Heb 11:32-33} and yet here he showeth some unbelief. Let us be faithful in weakness, though but weak in faith, and pray, "Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief" Albeit in some respects it was not amiss for Barak to desire Deborah’s company, viz., to advise him and pray for him, as being a prophetess. Neither fearful nor rash. Neque timide, neque temere, should be the soldier’s motto.
paragraphs.anchor: If thou wilt go with me.

paragraphs.text: Because a weak woman shall share with thee therein. Although in some women, such as were Deborah, Jael, Artemisia, Zenobia, Blandina, Queen Elizabeth, besides their sex there was nothing womanlike, or weak.
paragraphs.anchor: Shall not be for thine honour.

paragraphs.text: They followed him κατα παδας, in due order, and, as it were, treading in his steps. {See Trapp on "Jdg 4:6"}
paragraphs.anchor: And he went up with ten thousand men at his feet.

paragraphs.text: Who dwelt in the wilderness of Judah. {Jdg 1:16} Why he severed himself is not expressed; perhaps for better pasture’s sake, or it may be for conveniency of contemplation; for it is said in the next words, that he pitched his tent into the plain - or oak, or grove, as the Septuagint and others render it - of Zaanam. Bernard confessed of himself, that what knowledge of the Scriptures he had attained unto, he had got it in the woods and fields by meditation and prayer, Nullos se aliquando magistros habuisse nisi quercus et fagos, but the oaks and beech trees.
paragraphs.anchor: Had severed himself from the Kenites.

paragraphs.text: It was brought unto him either by public rumour,
paragraphs.anchor: And they showed Sisera.

paragraphs.text: “ Sine vano publica fama, ”
or else by intelligencers employed for the purpose: Habent enim Principes suos coricaeos. Mount Tabor also was a high hill, and not far from him.
"That ancient river," {Jdg 5:21} famous afterwards for the slaughter of the Baalites there. {1Ki 18:40}
paragraphs.anchor: Unto the river of Kishon.

paragraphs.text: As general of the army: yea, he alone is a whole army of men, van and rear both. {Isa 52:12}
paragraphs.anchor: Is not the Lord gone out before thee?

paragraphs.text: Or, Terrified, as the vulgar Latin hath it, perhaps by thunder and hailstones, as Jos 10:10 1Sa 7:10, where the same Hebrew word is used; or else by some hurry noise made in the air by the angels, as 2Ki 6:15-18; but something was certainly done from heaven, {Jdg 5:20} wherewith the Canaanites were so frightened, that many of them ran into the river Kishon and there perished. {Jdg 5:21} So the winds fought for Theodosius in that famous battle against Maximus. {a} Hence Claudian, a heathen, cried out of him -
paragraphs.anchor: And the Lord discomfited Sisera.

paragraphs.text: “ O nimium dilecte Deo, cui militat aether,
Et coniurati veniunt ad classica venti ”
{a} Aug., De Civ. Dei, lib. v. cap. 26.
Heb., Unto one. Ne ignifer quidem relictus est, as the Latin proverb hath it, {a} scarce one left to bring the sad news of a πανολεθρια.
paragraphs.anchor: There was not a man left.

paragraphs.text: “ Desinat elatis quisquam confidere rebus:
Magna repente ruunt, summa cadunt subito. ”
{a} Claudian.

i.e., Non erant simultates aut bella inter illos, {a} there was no open hostility: or if there were a league, the Emperor of the world, saith Ferus, had now disannulled it, as having proscribed Sisera, and declared that he should be destroyed, and that by a woman.
paragraphs.anchor: For there was peace

paragraphs.text: {a} Jun.
Fair words make fools fain: Vide cui fidas. Jael is commended by Deborah for what she did. {Jdg 5:24}
paragraphs.anchor: Turn in, my lord, turn in to me.

paragraphs.text: “ Dolus an virtus, quis in hoste requirat? ”
Stragula villosa, with a rug or blanket, to get him the sooner asleep.
paragraphs.anchor: She covered him with a mantle.

paragraphs.text: Ut esset potus suavior, et induceret illi somnum, saith Vatablus; that she might mend his liquor, and make him sleep; as it is the nature of milk, when drunk largely by them that are hot, to render them sleepy.
paragraphs.anchor: And she opened a bottle of milk.

paragraphs.text: An officious lie is held a peccadillo; but God’s children are such as will not lie. {Isa 63:8 Zep 3:13} Jael made him no promise to do as he desired, but said within herself, likely, as that good woman in Jerome did, Ideo mentiri nolo, ne peccem, I will do anything sooner than lie: for that were to sin against God.
paragraphs.anchor: That thou shalt say, No.

paragraphs.text: Which was long and strong enough for her purpose to pierce his skull, and to fasten him to the ground.
paragraphs.anchor: Took a nail of the tent.

paragraphs.text: Lo, there lay this proud worms’ meat sprawling, with his head fastened to the ground, as if it had been now listening what was become of the soul. In Eze 32:27, it is said, that such as cause terror in the land of the living, are tumbled together into hell.
paragraphs.anchor: And smote the nail into his temples.

paragraphs.text: Fright, and flight, and grief, and perhaps long watching, had cast him into a deep sleep: which made way to that somnus ferreus, as the poets call death.
paragraphs.anchor: For he was fast asleep and weary.

paragraphs.text: By the hand of woman, which those warriors take for no small disgrace. {Jdg 9:54} Heber was perhaps in the army of the Israelites. We read of a brave Hungarian woman whose courage far exceeded the weakness of her sex: for at the siege of Buda, she thrusting in amongst the soldiers upon the top of the fort, with a great scythe in her hand, at one blow struck off two of the Turks’ heads, as they were climbing up the rampart. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: Sisera lay dead.

paragraphs.text: {a} Turk. Hist., 741.
By the death of his general and destruction of his forces. See Jdg 4:16.
paragraphs.anchor: So God subdued on that day Jabin.

paragraphs.text: So let all thine enemies perish, O Lord. Read the Church’s prayer, Psa 83:9-10; - "Do unto them as to Sisera, as to Jabin, at the brook of Kison: which perished at Endor: they became as dung for the earth."
paragraphs.anchor: Until they had destroyed Jabin.
